title: Spots of time
hookLine: a lost boy, letters carved in the turf, a girl in the wind: moments that keep renewing us (The Prelude, book 12)
tomorrow: a tiger and a lamb. could the same hand have made both?

cards: Some memories show up uninvited, as sharp as the day they happened. Wordsworth said certain ones do something strange.
In The Prelude, the long poem of his own growing up, he writes: "There are in our existence spots of time, / That with distinct pre-eminence retain / A renovating virtue". Renovating: they repair us.
Then he tells the one he means. As a small boy riding in the hills, he lost his guide and came down alone to a place where a murderer had once been hanged. The gallows had rotted away.
Only letters, carved in the turf, remained.

teach.h: A POOL, A BEACON, A GIRL IN THE WIND.
teach.b: Frightened, he climbed away, and saw only plain things: a bare pool, a beacon on the hilltop, and a girl with a pitcher on her head, forcing her way against the wind. That's all. Nothing happened.
And yet the scene stayed, he says, with a visionary dreariness. Later, he came back to that same place in the happy days of early love, and the dreary spot gave him strength and radiance.
So do moments like that heal you, or haunt you? Readers of The Prelude argue it two ways, and Wordsworth gives both sides their lines.

teach.h: GIVEN: THE POWER IS IN THE MOMENT.
teach.b: Side one: the power is in the moment. The spot retains a virtue, something given, like grace, that you didn't make and can't manufacture. You can only receive it, and be grateful.
Side two: the power is in the mind returning.

teach.h: MADE: THE MIND IS LORD AND MASTER.
teach.b: Wordsworth also says these moments show that "The mind is lord and master", with the senses as its servant. The scene itself was bleak.
The mind, coming back to it changed, made it shine.
That's the teaching The Prelude leaves us: the past isn't fixed. A moment that came as fear can come back as strength, because of what it held, or because of who returns to it, or both.

how: Readers of Wordsworth return to The Prelude's spots of time as a way of reflecting on their own lives; some journaling and retreat practices ask people to write down one returning moment and reflect on it.

blemishes on the page of an old manuscript

games.q: the moment and the mind: tap the pairs.
p: Wordsworth's long poem of his growing up
the mind, with the senses as servant

s: Wordsworth's spots of time are all happy memories
his first one is dreary and frightening: a lost boy, letters in the turf, a girl in the wind.
Wordsworth says spots of time keep a renovating virtue
they repair the mind when ordinary life has worn it down.
The Prelude says the mind only receives what the senses give it
it says the mind is lord and master, with the senses as its servant.

games.q: you think the healing is in the moment itself, a gift. Theo thinks it's all in how the mind returns. what's the best case for his side?
o: Wordsworth says the mind is lord and master, and the dreary spot shone only when he came back.
memories are only brain chemistry, so nothing in them could ever be a gift.
Wordsworth admitted he made the spots of time up to fill out his poem.
games.why: the scene was bleak; it gave strength later, when he returned in love. that's Theo's best evidence. your side keeps the word virtue: something the spot retains.

practice: Take a pen and, in one line, write down a moment that keeps coming back to you: not the big event, just the scene, a road, a light, a face.
For two minutes, look at the line and ask what it has done for you, healed or haunted, or both.

wordCard.voice: Spots of time: Wordsworth's name, in The Prelude, for moments that stay with us and keep renewing us, even the dreary ones.

carryVoice: Your line: spots of time, and the mind that keeps returning to them. On we go.
